title: 'Likely' acute blood loss anemia after knee replacement
discharge_summary: SYNTHETIC CASE - NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient: Synthetic Patient 09, 70-year-old male. MRN: SYN-0009
Reason for admission: Elective right total knee arthroplasty for primary osteoarthritis of the right knee.

He underwent right total knee arthroplasty on the day of admission. Estimated blood loss was 600 mL. Hemoglobin was 13.4 g/dL before surgery and 8.2 g/dL on postoperative day 1. He was lightheaded with ambulation and was transfused 1 unit of packed red blood cells, with hemoglobin 9.3 g/dL the next morning and resolution of symptoms. He worked with physical therapy twice daily and was walking 150 feet with a walker at discharge.
1. Primary osteoarthritis, right knee, status post right total knee arthroplasty
2. Likely acute blood loss anemia, transfused 1 unit PRBC
Discharge plan: Home with home physical therapy. Aspirin 81 mg twice daily for 4 weeks for DVT prevention. Orthopedic follow-up in 2 weeks.
